reasoning_traces.think:
The core insight centers on the distinction between risk and uncertainty, where risk implies quantifiable probabilities and uncertainty denotes unknown unknowns. The interplay necessitates separating these domains mathematically to avoid conflating them in distributive theory. When factor combinations are infinitely divisible, all configurations yield equivalent outcomes—a symmetry that collapses into a monopoly condition under unlimited scalability. This reveals a fundamental duality: competitive markets require small, substitutable units of input, whereas monopolies arise when such divisibility fails. The failure mode emerges when theoretical models assume continuous variation but empirical systems exhibit discrete thresholds. In GSI, this manifests as Bayesian updating errors when prior beliefs do not account for non-stationary uncertainty. In GSE, it appears as state-space collapse during strategic transitions where firms fail to recognize scale-dependent feedback loops. The epistemological challenge lies in maintaining dualist logic across layers—neither treating uncertainty as risk nor assuming perfect divisibility in practice.
